jerusalem: City in the Southern Levant. It is one of the oldest cities in the world and is considered a holy city to the three major Abrahamic religions: Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
johannesburg: Largest city in South Africa. In 2022 (the year of the most recent census), the City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality had a population of 4,803,262, and the wider metropolitan area a population of 15,099,422, making it one of the 100 largest urban areas in the world.
juba: Capital and largest city of South Sudan. It has an area of 52 km2 (20 sq mi), with the metropolitan area covering 336 km2 (130 sq mi). Juba was established in 1920–21 by the Church Missionary Society (CMS) in a small Bari village, also called Juba.
k2: 2nd-highest mountain on Earth. K2, also known as Mount Godwin-Austen, at 8,611 metres (28,251 ft) above sea level, is the second-highest mountain on Earth, after Mount Everest at 8,849 metres (29,032 ft). It lies in the Karakoram range.
kabul: Capital and the largest city of Afghanistan. It is within the jurisdiction of Kabul District and has an estimated population of 5,333,284 people.
kaieteur-falls: Waterfall in the Essequibo. It then flows over a series of steep cascades that, when included in the measurements, bring the total height to 251 metres (822 ft). While many falls have greater height or greater flow, few have the combination of height and water volume.
kalahari-desert: Semi-arid sandy savanna in Southern Africa. The Kalahari Desert is a large semiarid sandy savanna in Southern Africa covering 900,000 km2 (350,000 sq mi), including much of Botswana, as well as parts of Namibia and South Africa.
kaliningrad: City in Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia. Kaliningrad (known as Königsberg until 1946) is the largest city and administrative centre of Kaliningrad Oblast, an exclave of Russia between Lithuania and Poland (663 kilometres (412 mi) west of the bulk of Russia). Located on the Pregolya River at the head of the Vistula Lagoon.
kampala: Capital and largest city of Uganda. The city proper has a population of 1,797,722 (2024 census) and is divided into the five political divisions of Kampala Central, Kawempe, Makindye, Nakawa, and Rubaga.
kangchenjunga: 3rd-highest mountain on Earth. It was first climbed on 25 May 1955 by Joe Brown and George Band, who were part of the 1955 British Kangchenjunga expedition.
karachi: Capital of Sindh, Pakistan. Situated at the southern tip of the country along the Arabian Sea coast, Karachi formerly served as the federal capital from 1947 to 1959.
karnak: Ancient Egyptian temple complex. It is part of the monumental city of Thebes, and in 1979 it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List along with the rest of the city.
kathmandu: Capital and largest city in Nepal. As per the 2021 Nepal census, it has a population of 845,767 residing in 105,649 households, with approximately 4 million people in the surrounding metropolitan area.
kazan: Capital city of Tatarstan, Russia. Kazan is the fifth-largest city in Russia, being the most populous city on the Volga and within the Volga Federal District.
khartoum: Capital of Sudan. With an estimated population of 7.1 million people, Greater Khartoum is the largest urban area in Sudan.
kigali: Capital and largest city of Rwanda. Founded in 1907 as a German administrative outpost, it served as a minor administrative centre until it became the national capital at independence in 1962, shifting the main administrative focus away from Huye (formerly Astrida). As of 31 August 2022.
kilauea: Active volcano in Hawaii. The volcano is between 210,000 and 280,000 years old and grew above sea level about 100,000 years ago.
kingston-jamaica: Capital and chief port of Jamaica. Kingston Parish had a population of 89,057, and St. Andrew Parish had a population of 573,369 in 2011 Kingston is only bordered by Saint Andrew to the east, west and north.
kingstown: Capital of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. With a population of 12,909 (2012), Kingstown is the most populous settlement in the country.
kinkaku-ji: Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan. It is designated as a World Heritage Site, a National Special Historic Site, a National Special Landscape, and one of the 17 Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.
kinshasa: Capital and most populous city of DR Congo. It is the most densely populated city in the DRC, the third-most populous city and third-largest metropolitan area in Africa, the world's seventh-most populous city proper (the most populous outside of China), and the fourth-most populous capital city in the world.
kitty-hawk: Town in North Carolina, United States. The population was 3,708 at the 2020 United States census.
kochi: Metropolis in Kerala, India. As of 2011, the Kochi Municipal Corporation had a population of 677,381 over an area of 94.88 km2, and the larger Kochi urban agglomeration had over 2.1 million inhabitants within an area of 440 km2, making it the largest and the most populous metropolitan area in Kerala.
kolkata: Capital of West Bengal, India. Kolkata is the seventh most populous city in India with an estimated city proper population of 4.5 million while its metropolitan region Kolkata Metropolitan Area is the third most populous metropolitan region of India with a metro population of over 15 million.
konark-sun-temple: 13th-century UNESCO world heritage site in Odisha, India. The temple is attributed to king Narasingha Deva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty about 1250 CE.
kosice: City in Slovakia. With a population of approximately 230,000, Košice is the second-largest city in Slovakia, after the capital Bratislava.
krakatoa: Volcanic caldera in the Sunda Strait, Indonesia. Two of them are known as Lang and Verlaten; another, Rakata, is the only remnant of an island, also called Krakatoa, mostly destroyed by an eruption in 1883 which created the caldera.
krakow: City in Poland. Its Old Town was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1978, one of the world's first sites granted the status.
kruger-national-park: First national park in South Africa. Areas of the park were first protected by the government of the South African Republic in 1898, and it became South Africa's first national park in 1926.
kuala-lumpur: Capital city of Malaysia. It is the most populous city in the country, covering an area of 243 km2 (94 sq mi) with a population of 2,111,536 as of 2026.
kumasi: City in Ashanti Region, Ghana. It is the second largest city in the country, with a population of 443,981 as of the 2021 census.
kuwait-city: Capital and largest city of Kuwait. Located at the heart of the country on the south shore of Kuwait Bay on the Persian Gulf, it is the political, cultural and economic primate city of the emirate, being home to the headquarters of most Kuwaiti corporations and the entirety of its banking system.
kyiv: Capital and largest city of Ukraine. As of January 2022, the population of Kyiv was 2,952,301, making it the seventh-most populous city in Europe.
kyoto: City in the Kansai region of Japan. Kyoto is one of the oldest municipalities in Japan, having been chosen in 794 as the new seat of Japan's imperial court by Emperor Kanmu.
la-boca: Barrio in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Today, it is mostly known for being home to Boca Juniors, one of the two largest sports clubs in Argentina.
la-paz: Seat of government of Bolivia. With 755,732 residents as of 2024, it is the third-most populous city in Bolivia.
la-rambla: Thoroughfare in Barcelona, Spain. A tree-lined pedestrian street, it stretches for 1.2 kilometres (3⁄4 mile) connecting the Plaça de Catalunya in its center with the Christopher Columbus Monument at Port Vell.
lagos: Most populous city in Nigeria. As of November 2025, the size of the city's population has been estimated to be between 17 and 21 million residents, making Lagos the largest city in Nigeria, the most populous urban area on the African continent, and one of the fastest-growing megacities in the world.
lahore: Capital of Punjab, Pakistan. It is the second-largest city in Pakistan, after Karachi, and 27th largest in the world, with a population of over 14 million.
lake-baikal: Freshwater rift lake in Russia. At 31,722 km2 (12,248 sq mi)—slightly larger than Belgium—Lake Baikal is the world's seventh-largest lake by surface area, as well as the second-largest lake in Eurasia after the Caspian Sea.
lake-balaton: Freshwater lake in Hungary. The Zala River provides the largest inflow of water to the lake, and the canalized Sió is the only outflow.
lake-chad: Lake in West-Central Africa. In the 19th century, it still had an area of 28,000 km2 (11,000 sq mi). However, due to climate change and human water diversion, the lake shrunk significantly between 1960 and 1990, the open water area decreasing from 25,000 km2 in 1960 to just 2000 km2 in 1980.
lake-como: Lake in Lombardy, Italy. At over 400 metres (1,300 ft) deep, it is one of the deepest lakes in Europe.
lake-constance: Lake in Germany, Switzerland and Austria. The nearby Mindelsee is not considered part of Lake Constance.
lake-geneva: Lake in Switzerland and France. It is one of the largest lakes in Western Europe and the largest on the course of the Rhône.
lake-ladoga: Lake in Leningrad, Russia. It is the largest lake located entirely in Europe, the second largest lake in Russia after Lake Baikal, and the 14th largest lake by area in the world.
lake-louise: Glacial lake in Banff National Park, Alberta, Canada. Lake Louise is named after the Princess Louise Caroline Alberta (1848–1939), the fourth daughter of Queen Victoria and the wife of the Marquess of Lorne, who was the Governor General of Canada from 1878 to 1883.
lake-malawi: Lake in Africa. It is the fourth largest freshwater lake in the world by volume, the ninth largest lake in the world by area and the third largest and second deepest lake in Africa.
lake-maracaibo: Body of water in Venezuela. With a surface area of 13,512 km2 (5,217 sq mi), if counted as a lake it would be the largest in South America, ahead of Lake Titicaca, as well as one of the oldest lakes on Earth, having formed 36 million years ago in the Andes Mountains.
lake-michigan: One of the Great Lakes of North America. It is the second-largest of the Great Lakes by volume (1,180 cu mi; 4,900 km3) and depth (923 ft; 281 m) after Lake Superior and the third-largest by surface area (22,300 square miles; 57,757 km2), after Lake Superior and Lake Huron.
lake-nicaragua: Largest lake in Central America. Of tectonic origin and with an area of 8,264 km2 (3,191 sq mi), it is the largest fresh water lake in Central America, the 19th largest lake in the world (by area) and the tenth largest in the Americas, slightly smaller than Lake Titicaca.
lake-ontario: Easternmost of Great Lakes in North America. It is bounded on the north, west, and southwest by the Canadian province of Ontario, and on the south and east by the U.S. state of New York.
lake-superior: Largest of the Great Lakes of North America. The northernmost, westernmost, and highest of the Great Lakes, Lake Superior straddles the Canada–United States border with the Canadian province of Ontario to the north and east and the U.S. states of Minnesota to the west and Michigan and Wisconsin to the south.
lake-tahoe: Lake in California and Nevada, United States. Lying at 6,225 ft (1,897 m) above sea level, Lake Tahoe is the largest alpine lake in North America, and at 122,160,280 acre⋅ft (150.7 km3) it trails only the five Great Lakes as the largest by volume in the United States.
lake-tanganyika: Rift lake in East-Central Africa. It is the world's second-largest freshwater lake by volume and the second deepest, in both cases after Lake Baikal in Siberia.
lake-titicaca: Large lake on the border of Peru and Bolivia. It is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.
lake-victoria: Lake in East-central Africa. With a surface area of approximately 59,947 km2 (23,146 sq mi), Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake by area, the world's largest tropical lake, and the world's second-largest fresh water lake by surface area after Lake Superior in North America.
lalibela: Town in Amhara Region, Ethiopia. The churches themselves date from the 7th to 13th centuries, and are traditionally dated to the reign of the Zagwe (Agaw) king Gebre Meskel Lalibela (r. c. 1181–1221). The layout and names of the major buildings in Lalibela are widely accepted, especially by local clergy.
las-vegas: Most populous city in Nevada, United States. It is the 24th-most populous city in the United States, with 641,903 residents at the 2020 census.
lausanne: City in Switzerland. The municipality of Lausanne has a population of about 150,000, making it the fourth largest city in Switzerland after Basel, Geneva, and Zurich.
leaning-tower-of-pisa: Bell tower in Pisa, Italy. The width of the walls at the base is 2.44 m (8 ft 0 in). Its weight is estimated at 14,500 tonnes (16,000 short tons). The tower has 296 or 294 steps; the seventh floor has two fewer steps on the north-facing staircase.
leeds: City in West Yorkshire, England. It is the largest settlement in Yorkshire and the administrative centre of the City of Leeds Metropolitan Borough, which is the second most populous district in the United Kingdom.
leipzig: City in Saxony, Germany. Leipzig is located about 150 km (90 mi) southwest of Berlin, in the southernmost part of the North German Plain (the Leipzig Bay), at the confluence of the White Elster and its tributaries Pleiße and Parthe.
lenin-s-mausoleum: Tomb in Moscow, Russia. From 1953 to 1961, it was named Lenin's and Stalin's Mausoleum.
lhotse: 4th-highest mountain on Earth. At an elevation of 8,516 metres (27,940 ft) above sea level, the main summit is on the border between the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and the Khumbu region of Nepal.
liberty-bell: Symbol of American independence and liberty. It was first called the Liberty Bell by members of the American abolitionist movement, who used it as a symbol.
libreville: Capital and largest city of Gabon. As of the 2013 census, its population was 703,904.
lille: Prefecture and commune in Hauts-de-France, France. The city of Lille proper had a population of 238,246 in 2023 within its small municipal territory of 35 km2 (14 sq mi), but together with its French suburbs and exurbs the Lille metropolitan area (French part only), which extends over 1,666 km2 (643 sq mi), had a population of 1,530,624 (2023).
lilongwe: Capital city and largest city of Malawi. It has a population of 989,318 as of the 2018 Ce, up from a population of 674,448 in 2008.
lima: Capital and largest city of Peru. The 2023 census projection indicates that the city of Lima has an estimated population of 10,092,000 inhabitants, making it the second-most populous city in South America after São Paulo and the largest Spanish-speaking city in the world in terms of city proper population.
lincoln-center: Performing arts venue in New York City. Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts (also simply known as Lincoln Center) is a 16.3-acre (6.6-hectare) complex of buildings in the Lincoln Square neighborhood on the Upper West Side of Manhattan.
lincoln-memorial: National memorial in Washington, DC. The memorial has been the site of many famous speeches, including Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech delivered on August 28, 1963, during the rally at the end of the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.
linz: Statutory city in Upper Austria, Austria. As of 1 January 2024, the city has a population of 214,064.
lisbon: Capital and largest city of Portugal. The western portion of its metro area, the Portuguese Riviera, hosts the westernmost point of Continental Europe, culminating at Cabo da Roca.
live-aid: 1985 benefit concert. The event was organised by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure to raise further funds for relief of the 1983–1985 famine in Ethiopia, a movement that started with the release of the successful charity single "Do They Know It's Christmas?" in December 1984.
liverpool: City in Merseyside, England. Liverpool rose to global economic importance at the forefront of the Industrial Revolution in the 19th century and was home to the first inter-city railway, the first non-combustible warehouse system (the Royal Albert Dock), and a pioneering elevated electrical railway.
ljubljana: Capital and largest city of Slovenia. Ljubljana (spoken Slovene: Lublana; also known by other historical names) is the capital and largest city of Slovenia, located along a trade route between the northern Adriatic Sea and the Danube region, north of the country's largest marsh, it has been inhabited since prehistoric times.
loch-lomond: Loch In Scotland. This occurs in the spring and autumn when the water column becomes uniformly mixed due to temperature-driven density changes Loch Lomond is 36.4 kilometres (22.6 mi) long and between one and eight kilometres (1⁄2–5 miles) wide.
loch-ness: Lake in Scotland. Loch Ness is best known for claimed sightings of the cryptozoological Loch Ness Monster, also known affectionately as "Nessie" (Scottish Gaelic: Niseag). Loch Ness lies along the Great Glen Fault, which forms a line of weakness in the rocks which has been excavated by glacial erosion.
lome: Capital and largest city of Togo. Its city limits extends to the border with Ghana, located a few hundred meters west of the city center, to the Ghanaian city of Aflao and the South Ketu district where the city is situated, had 160,756 inhabitants in 2010.
london-eye: Observation wheel in London, England. The structure is 135 metres (443 ft) tall and the wheel has a diameter of 120 metres (394 ft). When it opened to the public in 2000 it was the world's tallest Ferris wheel, until the 160-metre (525 ft) Star of Nanchang in China surpassed it in 2006.
london: Capital of England and the United Kingdom. London stands on the River Thames in southeast England, at the head of a 50-mile (80 km) tidal estuary down to the North Sea, and has been a major settlement for nearly 2,000 years.
long-march: 1934–1936 Red Army retreat during the Chinese Civil War. About 100,000 troops retreated from the Jiangxi Soviet and other bases to a new headquarters in Yan'an, Shaanxi, travelling approximately 10,000 kilometres (6,200 miles). About 8,000 troops ultimately survived the Long March.
los-angeles: Most populous city in California, US. It covers about 469 square miles (1,210 km2), and is the county seat and most populated city of Los Angeles County, which is the most populous county in the United States with an estimated 9.86 million residents as of 2022.
los-glaciares: National park in the Santa Cruz Province of Argentina. In 1981, it was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.
lotus-temple: Baháʼí House of Worship in New Delhi, India. Baháʼís in India first sought permission for a House of Worship in 1920, and the land at Bahapur was bought in 1954 under a plan set by Shoghi Effendi.
louvre: Art museum in Paris, France. In 1692, the building was occupied by the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres and the Académie Royale de Peinture et de Sculpture, which in 1699 held the first of a series of salons.
luanda: Capital and largest city of Angola. In 2024 the population reached more than 8.8 million inhabitants (a third of Angola's population). Among the oldest colonial cities of Africa, Luanda was founded in January 1576 as São Paulo da Assunção de Loanda by Portuguese explorer Paulo Dias de Novais.
lubumbashi: Second-largest city in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. No definite population figures are available, but the population of the city's urban area is estimated to be around 2,584,000 in 2021.
lugano: City in Switzerland. Lugano has a population (as of December 2020) of 62,315, and an urban agglomeration of over 150,000.
lusaka: Capital and largest city of Zambia. The founding of the modern city occurred in 1905 when it lay in the British protectorate of Northern Rhodesia.
luxembourg-city: Capital of Luxembourg. As of 31 December 2025, Luxembourg City has a population of 137,696 inhabitants, which is more than three times the population of the country's second most populous commune (Esch-sur-Alzette). The population consists of 160 nationalities.
luxor: City in southern Egypt. Luxor had a population of 284,952 in 2023, with an area of 43.0 km2 (16.6 sq mi) and is the capital of the Luxor Governorate.
lyon: City in France. The City of Lyon is the third-largest city in France with a population of 519,127 as of 2023 within its small municipal territory of 48 km2 (19 sq mi), but together with its suburbs and exurbs the Lyon metropolitan area had a population of 2,338,789 that same year, the second largest in France.
macau: Special administrative region of China. Formerly a Portuguese colony, the territory of Portuguese Macau was first leased to Portugal by the Ming dynasty as a trading post in 1557.
machu-picchu: 15th-century Inca citadel in Peru. Often referred to as the "Lost City of the Incas", Machu Picchu is one of the most iconic symbols of the Inca civilization and a major archaeological site in the Americas.
madeira: Portuguese archipelago in the North Atlantic. Madeira is an archipelago situated in the North Atlantic Ocean, in the region of Macaronesia, just under 400 kilometres (250 mi) north of the Canary Islands, Spain, 520 kilometres (320 mi) west of Morocco and 805 kilometres (500 mi) southwest of mainland Portugal.
madrid: Capital and largest city of Spain. The municipality covers an area of 605.77 square kilometres (233.89 sq mi). Madrid lies on the River Manzanares in the central part of the Iberian Peninsula at about 660 metres (2,170 ft) above mean sea level.
majuro: Capital of the Marshall Islands. The atoll has a land area of 9.7 square kilometers (3.7 sq mi) and encloses a lagoon of 295 square kilometers (114 sq mi). As with other atolls in the Marshall Islands, Majuro consists of narrow land masses.
makalu: 5th-highest mountain on Earth. Rising about 5 km (3 mi) north-northeast of the main summit across a broad plateau, and connected to Kangchungtse by a narrow, 7,200 m (23,600 ft) saddle, is Chomo Lonzo (7,804 m (25,604 ft)).
malabo: Former capital of Equatorial Guinea. It is located on the north coast of the island of Bioko (Bube: Etulá, historically known as Fernando Pó by the Europeans). In 2018, the city had a population of approximately 297,000 inhabitants.
malaga: Municipality in Andalusia, Spain. With a population of 592,346 in 2024, it is the 2nd-largest city in Andalusia and the 6th-largest in the country.
male: Capital of the Maldives. With a population of 211,908 in 2022 within its administrative area and coterminous geographical area of 1.9 square kilometres (0.73 sq mi), Malé is the most densely populated city in the world.
mallorca: Island in the Mediterranean Sea. The international airport, Palma de Mallorca Airport, is one of the busiest in Spain; it was used by 28 million passengers in 2017, with use increasing every year between 2012 and 2017.
malmo: City in Skåne County, Sweden. Located on the Öresund strait on the southwestern coast of Sweden, it is the largest city in Scania, with a municipal population of 365,644 in 2024, and is the gubernatorial seat of Skåne County.
managua: Capital and largest city of Nicaragua. Founded in 1819, Managua became the national capital in 1852.
manama: Capital and largest city of Bahrain. After periods of Portuguese and Persian control and a short invasion from the ruling dynasty of Saudi Arabia, followed by a longer invasion by Oman, Bahrain established itself as an independent nation in 1971 following a period of British hegemony.
manaus: Capital and largest city of Amazonas, Brazil. It is the seventh-largest city in Brazil, with an estimated 2024 population of 2,279,686 distributed over a land area of about 11,401 km2 (4,402 sq mi). Located at the east centre of the state.
manchester: City and metropolitan borough in England. The two cities and the surrounding towns form one of the United Kingdom's most populous conurbations, the Greater Manchester Built-up Area, which has a population of 2.87 million.
mandalay: City in Mandalay Region, Myanmar. Mandalay was founded in 1857 by King Mindon, replacing Amarapura as the new royal capital of the Konbaung dynasty.
manila: Capital of the Philippines. With 44,935 inhabitants per square kilometer (116,380/sq mi), Manila is one of the world's most densely populated cities proper.
manneken-pis: Brass sculpture and fountain in Brussels, Belgium. Manneken Pis is one of the best-known symbols of Brussels and Belgium, inspiring several legends, as well as numerous imitations and similar statues, both nationally and abroad.
maputo: Capital and chief port of Mozambique. The city has a population of 1,088,449 (as of 2017) distributed over a land area of 347.69 km2 (134.24 sq mi). The Maputo metropolitan area includes the neighbouring city of Matola, and has a total population of 2,717,437.
marina-bay-sands: Integrated resort in Singapore. At its opening in 2010, it was deemed the world's most expensive standalone casino property at S$8 billion (US$6.88 billion). The resort includes a 1,850-room hotel, a 120,000-square-metre (1,300,000 sq ft) meetings and conventions facility at Sands Expo & Convention Centre.
marrakesh: City in Marrakesh–Safi, Morocco. The red walls of the city, built by Ali ibn Yusuf in 1122–1123, and various buildings constructed in red sandstone afterwards, have given the city the nickname of the "Red City" or "Ochre City". Marrakesh grew rapidly and established itself as a cultural, religious.
marseille: City in southern France. Founded c. 600 BC by Greek settlers, Marseille is the oldest city in France, as well as one of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited settlements.
maseru: Capital and largest city of Lesotho. Maseru had a population of 330,760 in the 2016 census.
mashhad: City in Razavi Khorasan province, Iran. It has a population of about 3,400,000 (2016 census), which includes the areas of Mashhad, Taman, and Torqabeh.
matterhorn: Mountain in the Swiss and Italian Alps. It is a large, near-symmetric pyramidal peak in the extended Monte Rosa area of the Pennine Alps, whose summit is 4,478 metres (14,692 ft) above sea level, making it one of the highest summits in the Alps and Europe.
mauna-kea: Hawaiian volcano. Its peak is 13,803 feet (4,207.3 meters) above sea level, making it the highest point in Hawaii and the island with the second highest high point, behind New Guinea.
mbabane: Executive capital city of Eswatini. It has an estimated population of 94,874 (2010). It is located on the Mbabane River and its tributary the Polinjane River in the Mdzimba Mountains.
mecca: Holiest city in Islam and capital of Mecca Province, Saudi Arabia. The Great Mosque of Mecca, known as the Masjid al-Haram, is home to the Kaaba, believed by Muslims to have been built by Abraham and Ishmael.
medellin: City in Colombia. In 1616, the Spaniard Francisco de Herrera Campuzano erected a small indigenous village (poblado) known as "Saint Lawrence of Aburrá" (San Lorenzo de Aburrá), located in the present-day El Poblado commune.
medina: Second-holiest city in Islam and Capital of Medina Province, Saudi Arabia. The population as of 2022 is 1,477,023, making it the fourth-most populous city in the country.
mediterranean-sea: Sea between Africa, Asia, and Europe. The Mediterranean Sea covers an area of about 2,500,000 km2 (970,000 sq mi), representing 0.7% of the global ocean surface; it includes fifteen marginal seas, including the Aegean, Adriatic, Tyrrhenian, and Marmara.
meiji-restoration: 1868 return to imperial rule in Japan. The Restoration led to enormous changes in Japan's political and social structure and spanned both the late Edo period (often called the Bakumatsu) and the beginning of the Meiji era, during which time Japan rapidly industrialised and adopted Western ideas, production methods and technology.
melbourne: Capital city of Victoria, Australia. Its inhabitants are known as "Melburnians". The area of Melbourne has been home to Aboriginal Victorians for over 40,000 years.
memphis: City in Tennessee, United States. Situated along the Mississippi River, it had a population of 633,104 at the 2020 census, making it the second-most populous city in Tennessee, the fifth-most populous in the Southeast, and the 29th-most populous in the US.
mendoza: City in Argentina. As of the 2010 census [INDEC], Mendoza had a population of 115,041 with a metropolitan population of 1,055,679, making Greater Mendoza the fourth largest census metropolitan area in the country.
merlion: Official mascot of Singapore. The lion head represents Singapore's original name—Singapura—meaning "lion city" or "kota singa". The symbol was designed by Alec Fraser-Brunner, a member of the Souvenir Committee and curator of the Van Kleef Aquarium.
meteora: Rock formations and monasteries in Thessaly, Greece. As of December 2025, four of the original monasteries were occupied, in active use as monasteries that are managed by monks, and open to visitors: the monasteries of Great Meteoron (est. 1356), Varlaam, Holy Trinity, and Saint Stephen – the latter became a convent run by a community of nuns in 1961.
mexican-revolution: Nationwide armed struggle in Mexico (1910–1920). Although the decades-long regime of President Porfirio Díaz (1876–1911) was increasingly unpopular, there was no foreboding in 1910 that a revolution was about to break out.
mexico-city: Capital and most populous city of Mexico. Under the most recent definition agreed upon by the federal and state governments, Greater Mexico City had a population of 21,804,515, making it the world's 15th-largest metropolitan area and the second-largest urban agglomeration in the Western Hemisphere, after São Paulo.
mezquita-catedral-de-cordoba: Cathedral and former mosque in Córdoba, Spain. Among the most notable additions, Abd al-Rahman III added a minaret (finished in 958), and his son al-Hakam II added a richly decorated new mihrab and maqsurah section (finished in 971). The mosque was converted to a cathedral in 1236 when Córdoba was captured by the Christian forces of Castile.
miami: City in Florida, United States. Miami has the third-largest skyline in the U.S. with over 300 high-rises, 70 of which exceed 492 ft (150 m). It is the county seat of Miami-Dade County.
milan-cathedral: Cathedral church of Milan, Italy. It is the largest church in the Italian Republic—the larger St. Peter's Basilica is in the State of Vatican City, a sovereign state—and one of the largest in the world.
milan: Second-largest city in Italy. It is the second-largest city in Italy after the country’s capital, Rome, with a population of 1,362,863 in 2026.
minneapolis: City in Minnesota, United States. Minneapolis, Saint Paul, and the surrounding area are collectively known as the Twin Cities, a metropolitan area with 3.69 million residents.
minsk: Capital and largest city of Belarus. Minsk is one of the administrative capitals of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). First mentioned in 1067, Minsk became the capital of the Principality of Minsk, an appanage of the Principality of Polotsk.
moai: Monolithic statues on Easter Island. Nearly half are still at Rano Raraku, the main moai quarry, but hundreds were transported from there and set on stone platforms called ahu around the island's perimeter.
mogadishu: Capital and largest city of Somalia. The city has served as an important port connecting traders across the Indian Ocean for millennia and has an estimated urban population of 4,126,815.
mojave-desert: Desert in the southwestern United States. The Mojave Desert is often colloquially called the "high desert", as most of it lies between 2,000 and 4,000 feet (610 and 1,220 m). It supports a diversity of flora and fauna.
mombasa: City in Mombasa County, Kenya. It was the first capital of British East Africa, before Nairobi was elevated to capital status in 1907.
monrovia: Capital, chief port, and largest city of Liberia. Founded in 1822, it is located on Cape Mesurado on the Atlantic coast and, as of the 2022 census, had a population of 1,761,032 residents.
mont-blanc: Highest mountain in the Alps (4,806.m). It is the highest mountain in Europe outside the Caucasus Mountains, the second-most prominent mountain in Europe (after Mount Elbrus in Russia), and the 11th most prominent mountain in the world.
mont-saint-michel: Tidal island in Normandy, France. Mont-Saint-Michel and its surrounding bay were inscribed on the UNESCO list of World Heritage Sites in 1979 for its unique aesthetic and importance as a Catholic site.
monte-alban: Pre-Columbian archaeological site in Mexico. It has an elevation of about 1,940 m (6,400 ft) above mean sea level and rises some 400 m (1,300 ft) from the valley floor, in an easily defensible location.
monterrey: City in Nuevo León, Mexico. The city anchors the Monterrey metropolitan area, Mexico's second largest metropolitan area with a population of 5,347,000 as of 2026, ccording to the 2020 census, Monterrey proper has a population of 1,142,194.
montevideo: Capital and largest city of Uruguay. As of the 2023 census, the city proper has a population of 1,287,452, making up about 36.8% of the country's total population, in an area of 201 square kilometers (78 sq mi). Montevideo is situated on the southern coast of the country, on the northeastern bank of the Río de la Plata.
montpellier: Prefecture and commune in Occitania, France. Established in 1220, the University of Montpellier is one of the oldest universities in the world and has the oldest medical school still in operation, with notable alumni such as Petrarch, Nostradamus and François Rabelais.
montreal: Largest city in Quebec, Canada. Founded in 1642 as Ville-Marie, or "City of Mary", it now takes its name from Mount Royal, the triple-peaked mountain around which the early settlement was built.
monument-valley: Region of the Colorado Plateau, US. The most famous butte formations are located in northeastern Arizona along the Utah–Arizona state line.
moroni: Capital of Comoros. The city's estimated population in 2003 was 41,557 residents.
moscow-kremlin: Fortified complex in Moscow, Russia. The Moscow Kremlin, commonly known as the Kremlin, is a fortified complex (kremlin) in Moscow, Russia.
moscow: Capital and most populous city of Russia. The city covers an area of 2,511 square kilometers (970 sq mi); the urban area covers 5,891 square kilometers (2,275 sq mi); and the metropolitan area covers more than 26,000 square kilometers (10,000 sq mi). Moscow is among the world's largest cities: the most populous city entirely in Europe.
mosul: City in Nineveh Governorate, Iraq. It is the second largest city in Iraq overall after the capital Baghdad and situated on the banks of Tigris.
mount-ararat: Highest mountain in Turkey. The first recorded efforts to reach Ararat's summit were made in the Middle Ages, and Friedrich Parrot, Khachatur Abovian, and four others made the first recorded ascent in 1829.
mount-bromo: Somma volcano in Indonesia. At 2,329 meters (7,641 ft), it is not the highest peak of the massif, but is the most active and famous.
mount-cameroon: Active volcano in Cameroon near the Gulf of Guinea. It is the highest point in sub-Saharan western and central Africa, the fourth-most prominent peak in Africa, and 31st-most prominent in the world.
mount-elbrus: Highest mountain of Russia and Europe. It is a dormant stratovolcano rising 5,642 m (18,510 ft) above sea level, and is the highest volcano in Eurasia, as well as the tenth-most prominent peak in the world.
mount-erebus: Volcano on Ross Island, Antarctica. With a summit elevation of 3,792 metres (12,441 ft), it is the second most prominent mountain in Antarctica (after Mount Vinson) and the second-highest volcano in Antarctica (after the dormant Mount Sidley). It is the highest point on Ross Island, which is also home to three inactive volcanoes.
mount-etna: Active volcano on the east coast of Sicily, Italy. It is one of the tallest active volcanoes in Europe, and the tallest peak in Italy south of the Alps with a current height (September 2024) of 3,403 m (11,165 ft), though this varies with summit eruptions.
mount-everest: Earth's highest mountain. Its height was most recently measured in 2020 through a joint survey by Nepalese and Chinese authorities as 8,848.86 m (29,031 ft 8+1⁄2 in). Mount Everest attracts many climbers, including highly experienced mountaineers.
mount-fuji: Volcano in Japan. According to UNESCO, Mount Fuji has "inspired artists and poets and been the object of pilgrimage for centuries". UNESCO recognizes 25 sites of cultural interest within the Mount Fuji locality.
mount-hood: Stratovolcano in Oregon, United States. With a summit elevation of 11,249 feet (3,429 m), it is the highest mountain in the U.S. state of Oregon and is the fourth highest in the Cascade Range.
mount-kailash: Religious mountain in Tibet Autonomous Region in China. The peak of Mount Kailash is located at an elevation of 6,638 m (21,778 ft), near the western trijunction of China, India, and Nepal.
mount-kenya: Highest mountain in Kenya. The area was officially gazetted as the Mount Kenya National Park in 1949 and was later designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997 for its outstanding natural beauty and ecological significance.
mount-kilimanjaro: Mountain in Tanzania, highest in Africa. It is the highest mountain in Africa and the highest free-standing mountain above sea level in the world, at 5,895 m (19,341 ft) above sea level and 4,900 m (16,100 ft) above its plateau base.
mount-kinabalu: Highest mountain in Malaysia. With a height of 4,095 metres (13,435 ft), it is the third-highest peak of an island on Earth, the 28th-highest peak in Southeast Asia, and 20th-most-prominent mountain in the world.
mount-kosciuszko: Highest mountain in mainland Australia. It is located on the Main Range of the Snowy Mountains in Kosciuszko National Park, a part of the Australian Alps National Parks and Reserves, in New South Wales, and is located west of Crackenback and close to Jindabyne, near the border with Victoria.
mount-logan: Highest mountain in Canada. Although many shield volcanoes are much larger in size and mass, Mount Logan is believed to have the largest base circumference of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth.
mount-merapi: Active stratovolcano in Central Java and Yogyakarta, Indonesia. It is the most active volcano in Indonesia and has erupted regularly since 1548.
mount-nyiragongo: Active volcano in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The crater presently has two distinct cooled lava benches within the crater walls – one at about 3,175 m (10,417 ft) and a lower one at about 2,975 m (9,760 ft). Nyiragongo's lava lake has at times been the most voluminous known lava lake in most recent history.
mount-olympus: Highest mountain in Greece. In July 2026, the wider area of Mount Olympus was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as a mixed World Heritage Site, in recognition of its natural and cultural significance.
mount-pinatubo: Active stratovolcano in Luzon, Philippines. Pinatubo is known for its VEI-6 eruption on June 15, 1991, the second-largest terrestrial eruption of the 20th century after the 1912 eruption of Novarupta in Alaska.
mount-rainier: Stratovolcano in the U.S. state of Washington. At 14,406 ft (4,391 m) it is the highest mountain in the U.S. state of Washington, the most topographically prominent mountain in the contiguous United States, and the tallest in the Cascade Volcanic Arc.
mount-rushmore: Mountain with U.S. presidential sculptures. The sculptor, Gutzon Borglum, named it the Shrine of Democracy, and oversaw the execution from 1927 to 1941 with the help of his son, Lincoln Borglum.
mount-sinai: Mountain in the Sinai Peninsula. It is a 2,285-meter (7,497 ft) mountain near the city of Saint Catherine in the region known today as the Sinai Peninsula.
mount-st-helens: Volcano in Washington, U.S.. The eruption killed 57 people and destroyed 200 homes, 47 bridges, 15 miles (24 km) of railways, and 185 miles (298 km) of highway.
mount-toubkal: Highest peak of the Atlas mountain range. At 4,167 m (13,671 ft), it is the highest peak in Morocco, the Atlas Mountains, North Africa and the Arab world.
mount-vernon: Plantation estate of George Washington. The mansion was built of wood in a loose Palladian style; the original house was built in about 1734 by George Washington's father Augustine Washington.
mount-vesuvius: Active stratovolcano in the Gulf of Naples, Italy. It is regarded as one of the most dangerous volcanoes in the world, marked as one of the Decade Volcanoes, because 3,000,000 people live near enough to be affected by an eruption, with at least 600,000 in the danger zone.
mount-whitney: Highest mountain in the contiguous United States. The mountain's west slope is in Sequoia National Park and the summit is the southern terminus of the John Muir Trail, which runs 211.9 mi (341.0 km) from Happy Isles in Yosemite Valley.
mumbai: Capital of Maharashtra, India. As per the 2011 Census of India, it is the most populous city proper in India, with a population of almost 12.5 million, while the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, which is among the most populous metropolitan areas in the world, has a population of over 20 million.
munich: Capital of Bavaria, Germany. Munich is the largest city in Germany that is not a state of its own, and it ranks as the 11th-largest city in the European Union (EU). The metropolitan area has around 3 million inhabitants, and the broader Munich Metropolitan Region is home to about 6.2 million people.
murmansk: City in Murmansk Oblast, Russia. The city is a major port of the Arctic Ocean and is about 100 kilometres (62 mi) from the border with Norway, 180 kilometres (110 mi) from the border with Finland, and 1,930 kilometres (1,200 mi) from Moscow.
muscat: Capital and largest city of Oman. The metropolitan area includes six provinces, called wilayat, and spans approximately 6,500 km2 (2,500 sq mi). The Hajar Mountains dominate the view from Muscat.
mysore-palace: Historical palace in Mysore, Karnataka, India. The first palace to occupy the location was built in the 17th century during the reign of Kanthirava Narasaraja I, and was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times.
n-djamena: Capital and largest city of Chad. Originally called Fort-Lamy, it was founded in 1910 by the French during their colonization of Central Africa.
nagoya: Designated city in Aichi, Chūbu, Japan. It is the largest city in the Chūbu region, the fourth-most populous city in Japan (with a 2025 population of 2.3 million), and the principal city of the Chūkyō metropolitan area.
nairobi: Capital and largest city of Kenya. Nicknamed the "Green City under the Sun", Nairobi is uniquely notable for being the only capital city in the world that hosts a national park within its boundaries.
nanga-parbat: 9th-highest mountain on Earth. It rises far above its surrounding terrain and has the second-highest prominence among the 100 tallest mountains on Earth only behind Mount Everest.
nantes: Prefecture and commune in Pays de la Loire, France. The city is the sixth largest in France, with a population of 327,734 in Nantes proper (2023) and a metropolitan area of 1,050,815 inhabitants (2023). With Saint-Nazaire, a seaport on the Loire estuary, Nantes forms one of the main north-western French metropolitan agglomerations.
naples: Regional capital city of Campania, Italy. With a population of 905,050 within the city's administrative limits as of 2026, it is the largest city in southern Italy and the third-largest city in Italy after Rome and Milan.
nashville: Capital of Tennessee, United States. It is the 20th-most populous city in the United States and fourth-most populous city in the Southeast, with a population of 689,447 at the 2020 census (estimated at 721,074 in 2025). The Nashville metropolitan area, with over 2.15 million people, is the 35th-largest metropolitan area in the country.
nassau: Capital and largest city of The Bahamas. It is on the island of New Providence, which has a population of 296,522, 74.26% of the country's total population.
naypyidaw: Capital of Naypyidaw Union Territory, Myanmar. The city, previously known only as Pyinmana District, officially replaced Yangon as the administrative capital of Myanmar on 6 November 2005; its official name was revealed to the public on Armed Forces Day, 27 March 2006.
nazca-lines: Geoglyphs in the Nazca Desert, Peru. There are two major phases of the Nazca lines, Paracas phase, from 400 to 200 BC, and Nazca phase, from 200 BC to 500 AD.
neuschwanstein-castle: Palace in Bavaria, Germany. Since 2025, the castle has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "The Palaces of King Ludwig II of Bavaria: Neuschwanstein, Linderhof, Schachen and Herrenchiemsee". According to Guinness World Records, at 65 metres (213 feet), it is the tallest castle in the world.
nevsky-prospect: Thoroughfare in Saint Petersburg, Russia. Its name comes from the Alexander Nevsky Lavra, the monastery which stands at the eastern end of the street, and which commemorates the Russian hero Prince Saint Alexander Nevsky (1221–1263). Following his founding of Saint Petersburg in 1703.
new-delhi: Capital city of India. The foundation stone of New Delhi, south of central Delhi, was laid by George V during the Delhi Durbar of 1911.
new-orleans: Consolidated city-parish in Louisiana, US. With a population of 383,997 at the 2020 census, New Orleans is the most populous city in Louisiana, the second-most populous in the Deep South (after Atlanta), and the twelfth-most populous in the Southeastern United States; the New Orleans metropolitan area, with about 1 million residents.
new-york-city: Most populous city in the United States. With an estimated population of 8,586,038 as of 2026, distributed over 300.46 square miles (778.2 km2), New York is the most densely populated major city in the United States.
newcastle-upon-tyne: City in England. The settlement became known as Monkchester before taking on the name of a castle built in 1080 by William the Conqueror's eldest son, Robert Curthose.
newgrange: Neolithic monument in County Meath, Ireland. It is an exceptionally grand passage tomb built during the Neolithic Period, around 3100 BC, making it older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids.
ngorongoro-conservation-area: Protected area and a World Heritage Site in Arusha Region, Tanzania. Ngorongoro Conservation Area (UK:, US) is a protected area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Ngorongoro District, 180 km (110 mi) west of Arusha City in Arusha Region, within the Crater Highlands geological area of northeastern Tanzania.
niagara-falls: Waterfalls between the United States and Canada. Formed by the Niagara River, which drains Lake Erie into Lake Ontario, the combined falls have the highest flow rate of any waterfall in North America and the seventh largest in the world.
niagara-on-the-lake: Town in Ontario, Canada. Niagara-on-the-Lake is home to the oldest Catholic church, the second-oldest Anglican church in Ontario, and the oldest surviving golf course in North America.
niamey: Capital and the largest city of Niger. Niamey held Niger's first municipal elections in 1956, electing Djibo Bakary as the first mayor.
nice: Prefecture of Alpes-Maritimes, Southern France. Around 350 BC, Greeks of Marseille founded a permanent settlement and called it Nikaia, after Nike, the goddess of victory.
nicosia: Capital of the Republic of Cyprus. Three years after Cyprus gained independence from British rule in 1960, the Bloody Christmas conflict between Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots triggered island-wide intercommunal violence, and in 1964.
nile-delta: African river delta bordering the Mediterranean. From Alexandria in the west to Port Said in the east; it covers 240 km (150 mi) of the Mediterranean coastline and is a rich agricultural region.
normandy-landings: World War II landing operation in Europe. Codenamed Operation Neptune and often referred to as D-Day (after the military term), it is the largest seaborne invasion in history.
north-sea: Marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean. It is more than 970 kilometres (600 mi) long and 580 kilometres (360 mi) wide, covering 570,000 square kilometres (220,000 sq mi). It hosts key north European shipping lanes and is a major fishery.
notre-dame-de-paris: Cathedral in Paris, France, built 1163–1345. The construction of the cathedral began in 1163 under Bishop Maurice de Sully and was largely completed by 1260, though it was modified in succeeding centuries.
nottingham: City and council area in Nottinghamshire, England. Nottingham is a UNESCO "City of Literature". In the 2021 census, Nottingham had a reported population of 323,632.
nouakchott: Capital and the largest city of Mauritania. By the mid-1980s, Nouakchott's population was estimated to be between 400,000 and 500,000.
noumea: Capital and largest city of New Caledonia. As a result, the April 2025 census recorded a marked population decline for Nouméa, with only 173,814 inhabitants living in the metropolitan area of Greater Nouméa (French: agglomération du Grand Nouméa), down from 182,341 at the 2019 census, and 85,976 in the city (commune) of Nouméa proper.
novodevichy-convent: Monastery in Moscow, Russia. The convent was founded by Grand Duke Vasily III on May 13, 1524 in honor of the Smolensk Icon of the Mother of God "Hodegetria" - the main shrine of Smolensk, in gratitude for the capture of Smolensk in 1514.
novosibirsk: City and administrative centre of Novosibirsk Oblast, Russia. As of the 2021 census, it had a population of 1,633,595, making it the third-most populous city in Russia after Moscow and Saint Petersburg.
nuku-alofa: Capital of Tonga. It is located on the north coast of the island of Tongatapu, in the country's southernmost island group.
nuremberg-trials: Trials of Nazi German leaders. Between 20 November 1945 and 1 October 1946, the International Military Tribunal (IMT) tried 22 of the most important surviving leaders of Nazi Germany in the political, military, and economic spheres, as well as six German organizations.
nuremberg: City in Bavaria, Germany. First mentioned in 1050, Nuremberg developed around an imperial castle into one of the most important cities of the Holy Roman Empire.
nuuk: Capital and largest city of Greenland. The city was founded in 1728 by the Danish-Norwegian missionary Hans Egede when he relocated from the earlier Hope Colony (Haabets Koloni), where he had arrived in 1721; the governor Claus Paarss was part of the relocation.
odense: City in Denmark. The city was the seat of Odense County until 1970, and Funen County from 1970 until 1 January 2007, when Funen County became part of the Region of Southern Denmark.
odesa: City and administrative center of Odesa Oblast, Ukraine. On 25 January 2023, its historic city centre was declared a World Heritage Site and added to the List of World Heritage in Danger by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee in recognition of its multiculturality and 19th-century urban planning.
odz: City in central Poland. As of 2025, Łódź has a population of 639,890, making it the country's fourth largest city. Łódź first appears in records in the 14th century.
okavango-delta: River delta in Botswana. On 22 June 2014, the Okavango Delta became the 1000th site to be officially inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
ol-doinyo-lengai: Active volcano in Arusha Region, Tanzania. Eruptions in 2007–2008 affected the surrounding region.
opium-wars: 19th-century conflicts between China and European powers. The First Opium War was fought from 1839 to 1842 between China and the British Empire.
oran: Coastal city in Oran Province, Algeria. The total population of the city was 803,329 in 2008, while the metropolitan area has a population of approximately 1,500,000, making it the second-largest city in Algeria by population.
osaka: Designated city in Kansai, Japan. With an estimated population of 2.8 million as of October 1, 2025 and a population density of about 12,505 people per square kilometer, it is the largest component of the Keihanshin metropolitan area.
oscar-niemeyer-s-niteroi-museum: Art gallery in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The museum projects itself over Boa Viagem (“Bon Voyage,” “Good Journey”) beach and also a neighborhood, the 817 square metres (8,790 sq ft) reflecting pool that surrounds the cylindrical base “like a flower,” in the words of Niemeyer.
oslo: Capital and most populous city of Norway. Oslo was founded as a city at the end of the Viking Age in 1040 under the name Ánslo, and established as a kaupstad or trading place in 1048 by Harald Hardrada.
ostrava: City in the Czech Republic. Ostrava is the third largest city in the Czech Republic in terms of both population and area, the second largest city in the region of Moravia, and the largest city in the historical land of Czech Silesia.
ottawa: Capital city of Canada. Ottawa borders Gatineau, Quebec, and forms the core of the Ottawa–Gatineau census metropolitan area (CMA) and the National Capital Region (NCR). As of 2021, Ottawa had a city population of 1,017,449 and a metropolitan population of 1,488,307.
ouagadougou: Capital of Burkina Faso. Ouagadougou has one of West Africa's largest markets, which burned down in 2003 and has since reopened with better facilities and improved fire-prevention measures.
outback: Sparsely populated interior of Australia. In 2009, as part of the Q150 celebrations, the Queensland Outback was announced as one of the Q150 Icons of Queensland for its role as a "natural attraction".
oxford: City and district in Oxfordshire, England. The city is home to the University of Oxford, the oldest university in the English-speaking world; it has buildings in every style of English architecture since late Anglo-Saxon.
pacific-ocean: Largest ocean on Earth. At 165,250,000 square kilometers (63,800,000 square miles) in area (as defined with a southern Antarctic border), the Pacific Ocean is the largest division of the World Ocean and the hydrosphere and covers approximately 46% of Earth's water surface and about 32% of the planet's total surface area.
palace-of-the-parliament: Seat of the Parliament of Romania. The Palace reaches a height of 84 m (276 ft), is 92 m (302 ft) deep underground, has a floor area of 365,000 m2 (3,930,000 sq ft) and a volume of 2,550,000 m3 (90,000,000 cu ft). The Palace of the Parliament is the heaviest building in the world.
palace-of-versailles: Former royal residence in Versailles, France. The king, the court, and the royal government lived there permanently from 6 May 1682 until 6 October 1789, except during the Regency years (1715–1723). Conceived by Louis XIV to glorify the French monarchy.
palacio-barolo: Office building in Buenos Aires, Argentina. It stood as Buenos Aires' tallest building for more than a decade until the construction of the Kavanagh Building in 1936.
palacio-de-bellas-artes: Cultural centre in Mexico City. The initial design and construction was undertaken by Italian architect Adamo Boari in 1904, but complications arising from the soft subsoil and the political problem both before and during the Mexican Revolution, hindered then stopped construction completely by 1913.
palenque: Ancient Maya city-state in Chiapas, Mexico. It is located near the Usumacinta River in the Mexican state of Chiapas, about 130 km (81 mi) south of Ciudad del Carmen, 150 meters (490 ft) above sea level.
palermo: City in Sicily, Italy. From 831 to 1072 the city was under Arab rule in the Emirate of Sicily when the city became the capital of Sicily for the first time.
palikir: Capital city of the Federated States of Micronesia. A town of slightly above 5,000 residents, it is part of the larger Sokehs municipality, which had a population of 6,964 as of 2024, out of the nation's total population of 106,487.
palma-de-mallorca: City in the Balearic Islands, Spain. With a population of 438,234 as of 2024, it is the 8th-largest city in Spain.
pamukkale: Natural site in Denizli Province in southwestern Turkey. It was added as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988 along with Hierapolis.
panama-canal: Shipping route across Central America. A third, wider lane of locks was constructed between September 2007 and May 2016.
panama-city: Capital and largest city of the Republic of Panama. It has a total population of 410,354 in the city proper and 1,086,990 in the Panamá District, which includes the outer corregimientos of the city.
pantheon: Roman temple, later church, in Rome. The current Pantheon was built on the site of an earlier temple, which had been commissioned by Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa during the reign of Augustus.
papeete: Capital city of French Polynesia. It is the primary center of Tahitian and French Polynesian public and private governmental, commercial, industrial, and financial services, the hub of French Polynesian tourism and a commonly used port of call.
paramaribo: Capital and largest city of Suriname. The historic inner city of Paramaribo has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002.
paris: Capital of France. Haussmann's renovation of Paris, which created new boulevards, parks, and public works, gave birth to a modern city known as the "capital of the 19th century". Paris is a major railway, motorway, and air-transport hub; in 2024 Charles de Gaulle Airport was the EU's busiest airport.
park-guell: Public park system in Barcelona, Spain. In 1984, UNESCO designated the park a World Heritage Site, recognizing it as part of the "Works of Antoni Gaudí" collection and stating "the architecture of the park combined elements from the Arts and Crafts movement, Symbolism, Expressionism, and Rationalism.
park-of-monsters: Garden and sculpture complex in Italy. The Sacro Bosco ("Sacred Grove"), colloquially called Park of the Monsters (Parco dei Mostri in Italian), also named Garden of Bomarzo, is a Mannerist monumental complex located in Bomarzo, in the province of Viterbo, in northern Lazio, Italy.
parliament-hill: Home of the Canadian Parliament in Ottawa. Following several extensions to the Parliament and departmental buildings, and a fire in 1916 that destroyed the Centre Block, Parliament Hill took on its present form with the completion of the Peace Tower in 1927.
partition-of-india: 1947 division of British India. The partition involved the division of two provinces, Bengal and the Punjab, based on district-wide non-Muslim (mostly Hindu and Sikh) or Muslim majorities.
patagonia: Geographical region in South America. The Colorado and Barrancas rivers, which run from the Andes to the Atlantic, are commonly considered the northern limit of Argentine Patagonia.
pattaya: City in Chonburi, Thailand. It is on the east coast of the Gulf of Thailand, about 150 kilometres (93 mi) southeast of Bangkok, and has a population of 351,391 as of 2025.
peles-castle: Neo-Renaissance castle in Sinaia, Romania. It was constructed for King Carol I of Romania.
pelourinho: UNESCO World Heritage Site in Bahia, Brazil. Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Largo do Pelourinho retains a vibrant repertoire of colonial Portuguese architecture, exemplified by the Mannerist decoration of the Cathedral of Salvador.
perito-moreno-glacier: Glacier located in the Patagonian Andes. The 250 km2 (97 sq mi) ice formation, 30 km (19 mi) in length, is one of 48 glaciers fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field located in the Andes system shared with Chile which has a small part of the origins of the glacier.
persepolis: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire. It is one of the key Iranian cultural heritage sites and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
persian-gulf: Mediterranean sea in West Asia. The Persian Gulf has many fishing grounds, extensive reefs (mostly rocky, but also coral), and abundant pearl oysters; however, its ecology has been damaged by industrialization and oil spills.
perth: Capital city of Western Australia. The world's most isolated major city by certain criteria, Perth is part of the South West Land Division of Western Australia, with most of Perth's metropolitan area on the Swan Coastal Plain between the Indian Ocean and the Darling Scarp.
peterhof-palace: Series of palaces and gardens located in Petergof, Saint Petersburg, Russia. Francesco Bartolomeo Rastrelli completed an expansion from 1747 to 1756 for Elizabeth of Russia.
petra: Ancient rock-cut historical city in Jordan. The city is one of the New 7 Wonders of the World and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
petronas-towers: Interlinked supertall skyscraper in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The Petronas Towers remain the world's tallest twin skyscrapers, surpassing the original World Trade Center towers in New York City, and were the tallest buildings in Malaysia until 2019, when they were surpassed by The Exchange 106.
philadelphia: Most populous city in Pennsylvania, US. The Philadelphia metropolitan area, also known as the Delaware Valley, is located in both the Mid-Atlantic and northeastern United States; home to 6.33 million residents, it is the nation's ninth-largest metropolitan area.
phnom-penh: Capital of Cambodia. Founded in 1372, Phnom Penh succeeded Angkor Thom as the national capital in 1434 following the fall of Angkor, and remained so until 1497.
phoenix: Capital and most populous city of Arizona, U.S.. Phoenix is the county seat of Maricopa County in the Salt River Valley and Arizona Sun Corridor and, with an area of 517.9 square miles (1,341 square kilometers), is the largest city by area in Arizona and 11th-largest city by area in the United States.
phuket: Province of Thailand. Phuket province, encompassing an area of 547 km2 (211 sq mi), ranks as the second-smallest province in Thailand.
pico-de-orizaba: Highest peak in Mexico and highest volcano in North America. It rises 5,636 metres (18,491 ft) above sea level in the eastern end of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt, on the border between the states of Veracruz and Puebla.
pisa: Comune in Tuscany, Italy. The city is also home to the University of Pisa, which has a history going back to the 12th century, the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, founded by Napoleon in 1810, and its offshoot, the Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies.
pittsburgh: Second-most populous city in Pennsylvania, U.S.. The Pittsburgh metropolitan area has over 2.43 million people, making it the largest in the Ohio Valley and Appalachia, the second-largest in Pennsylvania, and the 28th-largest in the U.S. The greater Pittsburgh–Weirton–Steubenville combined statistical area includes parts of Ohio and West Virginia.
plaza-de-mayo: Public square in Buenos Aires, Argentina. On the occasion of the first anniversary of the May Revolution in 1811, the Pirámide de Mayo (English: May Pyramid) was inaugurated in the square's hub, becoming Buenos Aires' first national monument.
plaza-mayor: Square in Madrid, Spain. It was first built (1580–1619) during the reign of Philip III.
plymouth: City and unitary authority in Devon, England. It is located on the county's south coast between the rivers Plym and Tamar, about 36 miles (58 km) south-west of Exeter and 193 miles (311 km) south-west of London.
podgorica: Capital and largest city of Montenegro. Following the Allied victory in World War II, Podgorica was renamed Titograd in 1946, and simultaneously designated as capital of Socialist Republic of Montenegro.
pompeii: Ancient city near modern Naples, Italy. Along with Herculaneum, Stabiae, and many surrounding villas, it was buried under 4 to 6 m (13 to 20 ft) of volcanic ash and pumice in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD.
ponta-delgada: Municipality in Azores, Portugal. As of 2021, it has 67,287 inhabitants, in an area of 232.99 square kilometres (89.96 square miles). There are 17,629 residents in the three central civil parishes that comprise the historical city: São Pedro, São Sebastião, and São José.
popocatepetl: Stratovolcano in Puebla, Mexico. At 5,393 m (17,694 ft) it is the second highest peak in Mexico, after Citlaltépetl (Pico de Orizaba) at 5,636 m (18,491 ft). Popocatépetl is ranked 89th by prominence.
port-au-prince: Capital of Haiti. The city's population was estimated at 1,200,000 in 2022 with the metropolitan area estimated at a population of 2,618,894.
port-elizabeth: South African port city. Gqeberha was founded in 1820 as Port Elizabeth by Sir Rufane Donkin, who was the governor of the Cape at the time.
port-louis: Capital city of Mauritius. According to the 2018 census conducted by Statistics Mauritius, the population was 147,066.
port-moresby: Capital and largest city of Papua New Guinea. During World War II, it was a prime objective for conquest by the Imperial Japanese forces during 1942–1943 as a staging point and air base to cut off Australia from Southeast Asia and the Americas.
port-of-spain: Capital of Trinidad and Tobago. With a municipal population of 49,867 (2017), an urban population of 81,142 and a transient daily population of 250,000, it is Trinidad and Tobago's third largest municipality, after Chaguanas and San Fernando.
port-vila: Capital and largest city of Vanuatu. The mayor is Jenny Regenvanu of the Land and Justice Party, the first woman to hold the position, elected in August 2024.
portland: Most populous city in Oregon, U.S.. Located in the Pacific Northwest at the confluence of the Willamette and Columbia rivers, it is the 28th-most populous city in the United States, sixth-most populous on the West Coast, and fourth-most populous in the Pacific Northwest, with a population of 652,503 at the 2020 census.
porto-alegre: Capital and largest city of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. Its population of roughly 1.4 million inhabitants (2022) makes it the 11th-most populous city in the country and the centre of Brazil's fifth-largest metropolitan area, with 4.1 million inhabitants (2022). The city is the southernmost capital city of a Brazilian state.
porto-novo: Capital of Benin. In 1863, following British bombardment, Porto-Novo accepted French protection, and by 1900, it became the capital of French Dahomey.
porto: City in Portugal. On the Douro River estuary in northern Portugal, Porto is one of the oldest European centers, and its core was named a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1996, as the Historic Centre of Porto, Luiz I Bridge and Monastery of Serra do Pilar.
portsmouth: City in Hampshire, England. With a population last recorded at 208,100, it is the most densely populated city in the United Kingdom.
potala-palace: Fortress in Lhasa, Tibet. It was formerly the winter palace of the Dalai Lamas, and from 1649 until 1959 served as the Dalai Lamas' residence.
potosi: City in Bolivia. It is one of the highest cities in the world at a nominal 4,067 m (13,343 ft). Diego Huallpa, an indigenous prospector, is traditionally credited with the discovery of the Cerro Rico in 1545, which led to the founding and rapid growth of Potosí due to its extraordinary silver wealth.
potsdam-conference: 1945 Allied meeting on the postwar world. The Potsdam Conference (German: Potsdamer Konferenz) was held at Potsdam in the Soviet occupation zone from 17 July to 2 August 1945, to allow the three leading Allies to plan the postwar peace, while avoiding the mistakes of the Paris Peace Conference of 1919.
poznan: City in Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland. As of 2023, the city's population is 540,146, while the Poznań metropolitan area (Metropolia Poznań) comprising Poznań County and several other communities is inhabited by over 1.029 million people.
prado-museum: National art museum in Madrid, Spain. The numerous works by Francisco Goya, the single most extensively represented artist, as well as by Hieronymus Bosch, El Greco, Peter Paul Rubens, Titian, and Diego Velázquez, are some of the highlights of the collection.
prague-castle: Historic building in the Czech Republic. According to the Guinness Book of Records, Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle in the world, occupying an area of almost 70,000 square metres (750,000 square feet), at about 570 metres (1,870 feet) in length and an average of about 130 metres (430 feet) wide.
prague: Capital and largest city of the Czech Republic. Since 1992, the historic centre of Prague has been included in the UNESCO list of World Heritage Sites.
praia: Capital of Cape Verde. Located on the southern coast of Santiago island within the Sotavento Islands group, the city is the seat of the Praia Municipality.
pretoria: Executive capital of South Africa. The city is also a major global diplomatic hub; it is home to 134 foreign embassies and high commissions, representing the second-largest concentration of diplomatic missions in the world, surpassed only by Washington, D.C.
puerto-madero: Neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, Argentina. Puerto Madero has by far the highest property values of any barrio within Buenos Aires, surpassing the second-highest twofold.
puncak-jaya: Highest mountain in Indonesia and Oceania. However, since Puncak Jaya is in Western New Guinea, an area administered by Indonesia and therefore geopolitically part of Southeast Asia, the peak can also be considered the 8th highest mountain in this region, after Hkakabo Razi and six others in Kachin State, Myanmar.
punta-arenas: City in Magallanes y Antártica Chilena, Chile. Although the city officially was renamed Magallanes in 1927, its name was changed back to Punta Arenas in 1938.
pyongyang: Capital and largest city of North Korea. According to the 2008 population census, it has a population of 3,255,288.
quebec-city: Provincial capital of Quebec, Canada. This area was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1985 as the "Historic District of Old Québec".
queenstown: Resort town in New Zealand's South Island. It is the largest town in the Queenstown-Lakes District, and the primary administrative centre.
quito: Capital city of Ecuador. Quito's elevation of 2,850 meters (9,350 ft) makes it either the highest or the second-highest national capital city in the world.
rabat: Capital city of Morocco. Rabat is the country's seventh-largest city with a population of 515,619 (2024) and the second largest metropolitan area after Casablanca, with a population of approximately 2.1 million (2025). It is also the capital city of the Rabat-Salé-Kénitra administrative region.
recife: Capital city of Pernambuco, Brazil. It is the largest city in Pernambuco state, and the fourth-largest urban area in all of Brazil; the metro population of the city of Recife was 3,726,974 in 2022.
recoleta-cemetery: Cemetery located in Buenos Aires, Argentina. In 2011, the BBC hailed it as one of the world's best cemeteries, and in 2013, CNN listed it among the 10 most beautiful cemeteries in the world.
red-fort: Historical Mughal fort in Delhi, India. Serving as the main residence of the Mughal emperors, it was commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan on the 12th of May 1639; the fort was constructed following his decision to shift the Mughal capital from Agra to Delhi.
red-sea: Arm of the Indian Ocean between Asia and Africa. The Red Sea is the world's northernmost tropical sea and has been designated a Global 200 ecoregion.
red-square: Square in Moscow, Russia. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1990.
reims: Subprefecture and commune in Grand Est, France. Reims Cathedral, the adjacent Palace of Tau, and the Abbey of Saint-Remi were listed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991 because of their outstanding Romanesque and Gothic architecture and their historical importance to the French monarchy.
rennes: Prefecture and commune in Brittany, France. In 2023, the city had a population of 230,890 inhabitants, while the larger metropolitan area is the 10th most populated in France with a population of 789,516.
reykjavik: Capital and most populous city of Iceland. Reykjavík has a population of around 140,000 as of 2026, and the surrounding Capital Region has a population of around 252,000, constituting approximately 64% of Iceland's population.
riga: Capital and largest city of Latvia. Home to 588,911 inhabitants (as of 2026), the city accounts for a third of Latvia's total population.
rila-monastery: Eastern Orthodox monastery in Bulgaria. The monastery is named after its founder, the hermit Saint Ivan of Rila (876–946 AD), and houses approximately 60 monks.
rio-de-janeiro: Second-largest city in Brazil. It is the second-largest city in Brazil after São Paulo, and the largest by international tourists.
riyadh: Capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia. Riyadh had a population of 7 million people in 2022, making it the most populous city in Saudi Arabia, the fifth most populous in the Middle East, and the 38th most populous in Asia.
robben-island: Island in Table Bay, South Africa. He was later awarded the Nobel Peace Prize and was elected in 1994 as President of South Africa, becoming the country's first black president.
rock-of-cashel: Historic ecclesiastical site in Ireland. The Rock of Cashel (Irish: Carraig Phádraig [ˈkaɾˠəɟ ˈfˠaːd̪ˠɾˠəɟ]), also known as Cashel of the Kings and St. Patrick's Rock, is a historical site located dramatically above a plain at Cashel, County Tipperary, Ireland.
rock-of-gibraltar: Monolithic limestone promontory located in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar. Most of the Rock's upper area comprises a nature reserve which is home to about 300 Barbary macaques.
roman-aqueduct-of-segovia: Roman aqueduct in Segovia, Spain. The Old Town of Segovia and the aqueduct were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
rome: Capital and largest city of Italy. A special municipality named Roma Capitale with a population of 2.7 million in an area of 1,287.36 km2 (497.1 mi2), Rome is the third most populous city in the European Union by population within city limits.
rosario: City in Santa Fe Province, Argentina. Located 300 km (186 mi) northwest of Buenos Aires on the west bank of the Paraná River, it is the country's third-most populous city after Buenos Aires and Córdoba.
roseau: Capital and largest city of Dominica. Built on the site of the ancient Island Carib village of Sairi, it is the oldest and most important urban settlement on the island of Dominica.
roswell: City in Chaves County, New Mexico, US. It is home to the New Mexico Military Institute (NMMI), founded in 1891.
rothenburg-ob-der-tauber: Town in Bavaria, Germany. Between 1884 and 1903, Johann Friedrich von Hessing built the Wildbad spa in Rothenburg ob der Tauber.
rotterdam: City in South Holland, Netherlands. The Rotterdam–The Hague metropolitan area, with a population of approximately 2.7 million, is the 10th-largest in the European Union and the most populous in the country.
rovaniemi: City in Lapland, Finland. It is the 17th most populous municipality in Finland, and the 11th most populous urban area in the country.
royal-palace-of-madrid: Official residence of the Spanish royal family. With over 135,000 m2 (1,450,000 sq ft) of floor space and 3,418 rooms, the Royal Palace of Madrid is the largest palace in Western Europe, the largest royal palace in Europe, and among the largest palaces in the world.
russian-revolution: 1917–1922 civil war in the Russian Empire. It can be seen as the precursor for other revolutions that occurred in the aftermath of World War I, such as the German Revolution of 1918–1919.
rwandan-genocide: Mass murder campaign in Rwanda. The genocide was rooted in long-standing ethnic tensions, most recently from the Rwandan Hutu Revolution from 1959 to 1962, which resulted in Rwandan Tutsi fleeing to Uganda due to the ethnic violence that had occurred.
sack-of-rome: Siege and sack of Rome by the Visigoths. At that time, Rome was no longer the administrative capital of the Western Roman Empire, having been replaced first by Mediolanum (now Milan) in 286 and then by Ravenna in 402.
sacre-c-ur: Catholic basilica and landmark in Paris, France. The basilica was first proposed by the former Bishop of Nantes, Felix Fournier, in 1870, after France's defeat and Napoleon III's capture at the Battle of Sedan in the Franco-Prussian War.
sacsayhuaman: Archaeological site near Cusco, Peru. The site is an important example of Inca architecture and sits at an altitude of 3,701 metres (12,142 ft). The Spanish chroniclers recorded that within the Inca's oral history, the fortress was said to be built during the reign of Sapa Inca Pachacuti and his successors.
sagrada-familia: Basilica under construction since 1882 in Barcelona, Spain. In 2005, parts of the Sagrada Família (Nativity façade and Crypt) were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site, under "Works of Antoni Gaudí". On 19 March 1882, construction of Sagrada Família began under the architect Francisco de Paula del Villar.
sahara: Desert on the African continent. With an area of 9,200,000 square kilometres (3,600,000 sq mi), it is the largest hot desert in the world and the third-largest desert overall, smaller only than the deserts of Antarctica and the northern Arctic.
sahel: Biogeographical region in Africa. Since the 2010s, various coups, insurgencies, terrorist incidents, and foreign interventions have taken place across the Sahel and Françafrique, leading to the region being called the Coup Belt.
saint-basil-s-cathedral: 1561 Orthodox church in Moscow, Russia. It was built from 1555 to 1561 on orders from Ivan the Terrible and commemorates the capture of Kazan and Astrakhan.
saint-petersburg: Second-largest city in Russia. Saint Petersburg is the fourth-most populous city in Europe, the most populous city on the Baltic Sea, and the world's northernmost city of more than 1 million residents.
salamanca: Municipality in Castile and León, Spain. The University of Salamanca, founded in 1218, is one of the oldest in Western Europe, and the Old City of Salamanca is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, which every year attracts a significant number of students and cultural tourists.
salt-lake-city: State capital and largest city of Utah, U.S.. The population was 199,723 at the 2020 census, while the Salt Lake City metropolitan area has an estimated 1.3 million residents and is the 46th-largest metropolitan area in the United States.
salt-march: 1930 Indian protest led by Mahatma Gandhi. The march spanned 387 kilometres (240 mi), from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, which was called Navsari at that time (now in the state of Gujarat). Growing numbers of Indians joined them along the way.
salvador: Capital city of Bahia, Brazil. As the first capital of Colonial Brazil, the city is one of the oldest in the Americas.
salzburg: Capital of the state of Salzburg, Austria. The historic centre was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.
samarkand: City in southeastern Uzbekistan. Among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Central Asia, it has a population of 882,000 inhabitants as of 2026, making it the second-largest city in Uzbekistan after Tashkent.
san-diego: City in California, United States. It is the eighth-most populous city in the U.S. and second-most populous city in California with a population of over 1.4 million, while the San Diego area with over 3.3 million residents is the 18th-largest metropolitan area in the country.
san-francisco: City and county in California, US. San Francisco, officially the City and County of San Francisco, is the fourth-most populous city in California and the 17th-most populous in the United States, with a population of 826,079 in 2025.
san-jose: Capital and largest city of Costa Rica. San José is simultaneously one of Costa Rica's cantons, with its municipal land area covering 44.62 square kilometers (17.23 square miles) and having within it an estimated population of 352,381 people in 2022.
